name: MS-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Bennie Thompson's long incumbency and large cash advantage
model.rationale: Thompson holds a D+11 district with a two-decade incumbency, a $1.4M war chest against a challenger who raised under $50k, and no outside spending against him. Markets price him near certain, and no evidence suggests a competitive race.
model.watch: Any late polling or outside spending targeting Thompson would be the first sign of trouble, but none is currently present.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Bennie Thompson has represented this Mississippi Delta district for decades, and the seat remains firmly Democratic with an 11-point partisan lean. He enters the general election with roughly $1.4 million on hand after raising about $770,000 this cycle, while Republican Ron Eller has raised under $50,000 and has minimal cash. No outside groups are spending in the race, and no general-election polls are available.

Prediction markets give Thompson roughly a 97% chance of winning, and no expert raters list the race as competitive. The fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit margin, consistent with Thompson's history of easy reelections in this seat.
